ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Domestic call charges 
*441. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: 
SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be 
please to state: 
(a) whether TRAI has decided to do away with levying Access Deficit Charges (ADO or 
telecom operators as a result of which domestic call (Local and STD) charges would become 
cheaper; and 
(b) if so, to what extent domestic calls are likely tc become cheaper and the likely new 
rates to be fixed by various telecom operators, including the BSNL and MTNL, and by when 
are they likely to be made effective? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI A. RAJA): (a) and (b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has decided to do away 
with the levying of Access Deficit Charges (ADC) which was being charged at a rate of 
0.75% of Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR) on telecom operators for domestic segments w.e.f. 
1.4.2008. However, ADC on incoming International Long Distance Calls has been reduced 
from Rupee I per minute to Rupee 0.50 per minute w.e.f. 1.4.2008 and is to be phased out 
from 30.09.2008. 
As per the existing provisions of Telecommunications Tariff Orders (TTO), tariff for 
telecom services are under forbearance, except with regard to Fixed Line Service in Rural 
Areas, National Roaming Service in Cellular Mobile Service and Leased line Service. The 
reduction in levy is of the order of 0.75% of AGR and its impact on domestic call charges is 
less than 0.75%. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Question 441 please. 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, if it is possible Question No. 448 also, if the hon. Member is present, 
may be clubbed together. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASE KHAR: Sir, the go od thing is that the ADC regime is 
being shut down almost five years after I first pointed out to the regulator of the Government 
how some companies, big and small, were exploiting this ADC regime and illegally making 
hundreds of crores of rupees at the cost of the country using grey market international calls. 
So, I compliment the TRAI and the Government for taking this decision and plugging this 
loophole even if it has been done so belatedly. 
Sir, my first question relates to the real objective of the ADC and the USO Fund which is 
for rural tele density. TRAI has recommended that Rs. 2,000 crores be given to the BSNL 
from the USO Fund in lieu of the ADC for increasing rural tele density. I wholeheartedly 
support that. But, my question is a broader one, Sir. What is the Government's explanation

for the poor performance with regard to the growth of the rural tele density compared to 
urban tele density in the last few years? Despite the availability of significant resources in 
the USO Fund, how much has been disbursed to the BSNL from the USO and others and 
why has the USO's peiformance been so unsatisfactory?  
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, as the hon. Member has put it, in order to improve the rural tele 
density, the USO Fund is being spent invariably through all service providers. Of course, the 
rural telephones are be ing owned 95 per cent by the BSNL. So, automatically, more funds 
share will go to the BSNL. It is true that out of the collection that has been made as on 
01.04.2008, the amount being accumulated is Rs. 2039392 crore out of which only 
Rs. 6371.435 crores have been spent in the USO Fund. Now, for the current financial year, 
the Government has prDcessed all formalities to put up 8,000 towers across the country. Not 
only that, for the coming years, for 11,000 towers, places are being identified. Putting together, 
around 18,000 towers are going to be put up by the USO Fund. The process is almost over, 
As soon as the towers are put up, the services will be started in rural areas. Of course, the 
rural tele density is very low. While urban tale density is around 60 per cent, rural tele 
density is only 7.8 per cent. The Government is deeply concerned. We are pushing all operators 
to go for the rural areas. Of course, there is no rule or condition in the TRAI recommendations 
that all the operators should mandatorily go for the rural areas. However, all this message is 
being taken up as the hon. Member has put it. Under the USO Fund, we hope, in the course 
of time, within a year, rural tele density will improve.  
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir, my second question pertains to the general 
performance of the BSNL which is a PSU we all have been proud of but increasingly we are 
not. Why is the BSNL's market share in performance is reducing every year? Will the 
Government be a silent spectator to this trend which is continuing till it become sick and 
irrelevant like many other PSUs, or, will it take decisive steps to enable BSNL to increase its 
market share and become a stronger player? And, if so, what are the steps the Government is 
considering? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the performance of any company, including the Government PSUs, 
depends upon the market forces. The Government can safeguard certain areas like rural 
services through USO Fund or others. Of course, first time, the Government is deeply 
concerned to wipe out the AGR which is being collected for the rural telephones also. The 
hon. Member may be aware that there is a system through which we are collecting 5 per cent 
from the USO Fund and invariably 2 or 3 per cent from all private operators out of their net 
profit. 
SHRI A. RAJA: This year, so far as the rural telephones owned by BSNL and by other 
service providers are concerned, we are considering that there will be no licence fee for 
landline connections! For that, a reference has been made to the Telecom Commission. It is 
being deliberated. If it is passed by the Telecom Commission, I hope , more than Rs. 1000 
crore will be saved by the BSNL. It will be an incentive to the BSNL. So, these types of 
incentives can be extended to the BSNL. But, the market forces will decide the standing of 
these companies —first place, second place or third place. It will be determined by the 
market forces. 
SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Sir, the Government does not have any control over the 
telephone operators. I am sorry to say that. On 3rd December, regarding the tariffs, the 
Minister told this august that it is for TRAI to see whether the tariffs need to be fixed. But,

foreign players are also coming.

SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Sir, I am putting. The foreign players are coming with 
huge premiums, but, the Indian telecom operators are not proportionately reducing the tariffs. 
Why is it so? And even after doing away with the ADC, the reply of the Minister is vague. 
Some providers limited the reduction to their net calls instead of all types of calls. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Please put your supplementary question. 
SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Sir, I am putting my question. From mobile to landline,

My question is: Has the Minister developed any mechanism to ensure that all the Jcisions 
of TRAI are implemented in true earnestness? 
SHRI A. RAJA: Sir, the answer to the first part of the question is, yes, it is true that there 
is no tariff fixation in this country. The tariff is regulated by a regulator, namely, the Telecom 
Regulatory Athority of India. The concept which is adopted by TRAI is the concept of 
forbearance. The market forces and the level pyaying field will decide what type of packages 
can be given to the consumers. Of course, the Government has a second opinion on that. 
That is why, in December, in the same House, I observed that, if necessary, the matter can be 
taken up with TRAI again. The matter is being processed. We want to fix up a tariff or we 
have to give a fair and level playing field in this country. 
Sir, with all sincerity, I have to share with this House that after 1993, only this Government 
permitted more and more competition under the advice of the hon. Prime Minister. We 
permitted five to seven more operators so that there will be a healthy level playing field once 
the roll-out starts. Once the roll-out starts, as a Minister, optimistically, I foresee that the 
tariffs will come down by 50 per cent. 
The second part of the question is with re gard to ADC. There is no discrimination. 
Regarding TRAI recommendations also, the recommendatory body has every right to give 
recommendations. The recommendations must be appraised by the Telecom Commssion 
and there after, we will see what type of  recommendations can be accepted. Suppose, we 
have a deviation with the recommendation that has been made by TRAI, the Ministry is 
entitled to refer the matter b ack to TRAI. It does not mean that the recommendation of the 
TRAI is completely sacrosanct and it has to be accepted in toto. Yes, we admit some 
recommendations. And if we have reservati ons on some recommendations, we refer the 
matter back toTRAI. We have already refe rred back certain recommendations. Some 
recommendations are still under consideration and we will come out with the solutions. 
SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: But, what about this issue? 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Please, You have asked your supplementary. 
SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: But, Sir, it has not been answered.

8    Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA] to Questions 
Statement 
(a) and (b) No, Sir. The forest cover of the country has more or less stabilized. The forest 
covers of the country as per 2001, 2003 and 2005 assessments is given below: 
 
Assessment Year 2001 2003 2005 
Forest Cover (in km2) 653,898 677,816 677,088 
It can be seen that the forest cover of the country has increased by 23,918 km2 between 
2001 and 2003 assessments, and decreased marginally by 728 km2 between 2003 and 2005      
assessments. 
The Forest Survey of India (FSI) carries out forest cover assessment of the country using 
remote sensing technology once every two years. 
(c) and (d) No, Sir. No such evaluation for decrease in forest cover has been done through 
Joint Forest Management. The protection offered by the Joint Forest Management Committees 
contribute to regeneration of forests which may lead to increase in forest cover. In addition, 
the Integrated Forest Protection Scheme being implemented by the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests, provides financial support to the State/UT Governments for activities 
encouraging 
forest protection.

Biological diversity 
*447. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 the various measures to popularise the concept of Biological diversity. 
 the various kinds of institutions concerned over Research and Development of Bio- 
diversity and the role of the National Bio-diversity Authority; and 
 whether the conservation aspect of Bio-diversity would offend or put a hurdle on the 
growth and development of medicinal plants, herbal plants used for health care? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI N AMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) The Government has taken a number of measures to 
popularise the concept of conservation of biological diversity which include introduction of 
curricula in the educational institutions and generation of awareness through a scheme on 
'Environmental Education, Awareness and Training'. The components under this scheme are. 
National Green Corps Programme, National Environment Awareness Campaign, organizing 
of seminars, workshops and training courses, generating awareness through mass media and 
providing grants-in-aid to pr ofessional bodies to achieve this objective. Institutions under 
the Central Government such as the various forest institutes, the Botanical and Zoological 
Surveys of India promote knowledge about the different flora and fauna of India which 
make up bio-diversity. Besides, the State Governments, institutions in the private sector and 
Non-Governmental Organizations have also been undertaking activities for popularising the 
various aspects of conservation of bio-diversity. 
(b) Institutions under the Central Government such as the Botanical Survey of India, the 
Zoological Survey of India, the Indian Council of Forestry  Research and Education, the 
G.B. Pant Institute of Himalayan Environment and Development, the Salim Ali Centre for 
Ornithology and Nature and the Wildlife Institute of India, institutions under the State 
Governments and the private sector, through in-house and sponsored projects are carrying 
out research on multi disciplinary aspects of bio-diversity conservation. The National Bio- 
diversity Authority has been established under the Biological Diversity Act 2002 with the 
aim to lay down procedures and guidelines to conserve bio-diversity, promote sustainable 
use, and ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of biological 
resources and associated knowledge, to advise the Central Government on matters related to 
bio-diversity, create awareness among the masses and coordinate the activities of the State 
Bio-diversity Boards.

Steps to reduce urban poverty 
*450. SHRIS. ANBALAGAN: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
 the number of below poverty line (BPL) people living in the urban areas of the country 
at present, State-wise; 
 the percentage of BPL people in the total population of urban areas, State-wise; 
 the reasons for continuous poverty of large number of people despite the schemes of 
the Union Government to improve their lives; and 
 the concrete steps proposed to be taken by the Union Government to reduce the 
increasing urban poverty in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) Planning Commission release 
estimates of urban poor from time to time based on the national sample surveys conducted 
by the National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO). The National Sample Survey 
Organisation (NSSO) has conducted the latest large sample survey on household consumer 
expenditure (61st Round), covering the period July 2004 to June 2005. From this data, two 
different consumption distributions for the year 2004-05 have been obtained. The first one 
is from the consumption data collected using 30-day recall period for all the items. The other 
distribution is obtained from the consumer expenditure data collected using 365-day recall 
period for five infrequently purchased non-food items, namely clothing, footwear, durable 
goods, educations and institutional medical expenses and 30-day recall period for the 
remaining items. These two consumption distribution have been termed as Uniform Recall 
Period (URP) consumption di stribution and Mixed Recall Period (MRP) consumption 
distribution respectively. The Planning Commission has estimated poverty in 2004-05 using 
both the distributions. As per these estimates, number and percentage of urban poor both by 
MRP method as well as URP method, State-wise, are at the Statement(See below). 
 The reasons for continuous poverty in large number of cities and towns include various 
factors such as natural increase in the urban poor population, migration of poor people from 
rural areas to urban areas, lack of basic amenities including affordable housing to low income 
segments, inadequate employment opportunities generated by the organized sector etc. 
Moreover, budgetary allocations under various governmental schemes, till the launching of 
Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) in December, 2005, have 
been meagre. 
 The Government of India has adopted a two pronged approach to address the issue of 
increasing urban poverty in the country: 
(i) A large component of Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission 
(JNNURM) namely Basic Services to th e Urban Poor (BSUP), applicable to 
63 identified cities and Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme 
(IHSDP), applicable to other cities and towns, provide additional central assistance 

Written Answers to [24 APRIL 2008] Starred Questions   25 
for construction of houses and provision of basic amenities to the urban poor. A 
sum of Rs. 18,100 crores has been allocated for the Basic Services to the Urban 
Poor (BSUP) and Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme (1HSDP) 
components for the Mission period (2005-2012). Further, emphasis is placed under 
JNNURM on reforms at State and urban local body levels to ensure provisions of 
land for affordable housing, earmarking of municiple budget for the urban poor 
and time-bound programme for provisions of seven basic amenities. 
(ii) The allocation under Swarna Jaya nti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)—a 
programme under which provision is made for self-employment through setting 
up of micro-enterprises by individuals as well as women groups; wage employment 
to the urban poor through creation of socially and economically useful public 
assets; skill upgradation training; and community empowerment for facilitating 
the organisation of the urban poor—has been increased substantially from 
Rs. 160 crore in 2005-2006 to Rs. 250 crore in 2006-2007, Rs. 344 crore in 
2007-2008 and Rs. 515 crore in 2008-09.

Housing policy and regulatory measures for real estate 
*453. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
 whether there is a national policy on housing as the land prices are soaring and the 
entry of FDI in real estate has made housing out of reach of the ordinary people including 
the middle class; 
 whether there is any proposal with Government to regulate private sector in the real 
estate; and 
 the regulatory measures contemplated by Government for the real estate? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) The first ever urban focused National 
Urban Housing and Habitat Policy (NUHHP), 2007 was laid on the Table of both Houses of 
the Parliament on 7.12.2007. The Policy has been widely circulated ampngst various State 
Governments/Union Territories and other stakeholders. 
The Policy seeks to bridge the gap between need and supply of housing and infrastructure 
and inter-alia provides for accelerating the pace of development of housing and related 
infrastructure; and creating an adequate and affordable housing stock both on rental and 

Written Answers to [24 APRIL 2008] Starred Questions   29 
ownership basis. The Policy also seeks to promote the use of proven and cost-effective 
building materials and technology to bring down construction costs. Further, the Policy 
encourages State Governments/Development Authorities to periodically review their master 
plans and zonal plans and facilitate accelera ted supply of serviced land for housing with 
particular focus on the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Group (LIG) 
and also make special provisions for the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes/Minorities/ 
Disabled and Women. 
The Policy refers to use of innovative spatial incentives by providing that 10 to 15 per cent 
of land in every new public/private housing project or 20 to 25 per cent of Floor Space Index 
(FS1), whichever is greater be reserved for EWS/LIG housing. Further the Policy seeks that 
Urban Local Bodies in consultation with all stake-holders will enforce regulatory measures 
for planned development in an effective manner and prepare master Plans and Metropolitan 
Plans in consonance with the concerned District Plan and the State Regional Plan. These 
measures are likely to stem the rate of growth of housing prices. 
(b) and (c) The Government has not taken any decision on regulatory measures in real 
estate including regulation of the private sector in the real estate on an all India basis.

3244. SHRI BJ. PANDA:

(c) whether it is proposed to develop a suitable emergency response mechanism specific

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (SHRI SANTOSH 
BAGRODIA): (a) and (b) Monitoring of safety parameters in coal mines is primarily the 
responsibility of mine operators. The coal companies have established Internal Safety 
Organisation (ISO) for effective monitoring of safety aspects covering mine level, area level

Ministry of Labour and Employment is vested with the responsiblity for monitoring of safety

emergency such as inundation, fires and explosion as per the provisions of Coal Mines 
Regulations. Standing orders delineating the actions and persons responsible for various 
activities in time of emergency like inundation, fires and explosion are issued by the colliery 
management including the role of rescue personnel. A Crisis Management Plan in case of 
disasters is also put in place at Government level.

50    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Unstarred Questions 
Statement-I 
Salient features of "The Telecom Unsolicited Commercial Communication Regulations, 
2007", dated 5th June, 2007 and its amendment dated 17th March, 2008 regarding 
Regulation 16 and 17 to check unwanted calls 
(i) For not receiving Unsolicited Commercial Communication (UCC) calls a 
subscriber has to register with National Do Not Call Registry (NDNC). 
(ii) In case a subscriber receives any Unsolicited Commercial Communication (UCC) 
after expiry of forty five days of his request of registration in the NDNC, he 
can make a complaint mentioning the call originating number to his service 
provider. 
(iii) The service provider after verification, forward the complaint to the service 
provider from whose network such UCC originated. 
(iv) If the originating access provider finds that the call is a UCC then he shall direct 
the sender to forthwith discontinue the sending of such a UCC to the complainant. 
(v) In case the sender of the UCC sends UCC again the originating access provider 
shall charge higher tariff in respect of such UCC. 
(vi) The TRAI through Telecom Tariff Order (Forty Seventh Amendment) 2008 has 
notified tariff of Rs. 500 for first such UCC and Rupees 1000 for second 
(subsequent) UCC. 
(vii) Disconnection of the telecom facilities of the telemarketer by the Service Provider 
if UCC is not stopped even after imposition of the prescribed Rs. 500 and 
Rs. 1000 tariff by the Service Provider. 
(viii) If the originating access provider finds that the sender has made UCC again after 
having charged at the specified rate, the originating access provider shall disconnect 
the telephone of such sender. 
(ix) No service provider shall also send UCC to its subscriber who has made a request 
for registration in the NDNC. 
(x) If service provider fails to act as per the regulation, it will be charged with a 
financial disincentive not exceeding Rs. 5000/- for first such instance and not 
exceeding Rs. 20000/- for each subsequent violation. 
Statement-II 
Salient features of "The Telecom Unsolicited Commercial Communication Regulations, 
2007", dated 5th June, 2007 regarding regulation 13, 14 and 15 to check unwanted calls 
(i) Every Telemarketer is required to be registered by the Department of Telecommuni- 
cations. 
(ii) In case the telemarketer fails to register with the Department of 
Telecommunications, his telephone connection shall be disconnected or provision 
of telecom service be discontinued by the Access Service Provider. 

Written Answers to [24 APRIL 2008] Unstarred Questions   51 
(iii) While providing telephone connections/service, the Access Service Provider shall 
obtain an undertaking from the Telemarketer to the effect that he agrees not to 
make Unsolicited Commercial Communication (UCC) to any subscriber whose 
telephone number appears on National Do Not Call Register. 
(iv) In case the telemarketer fails to give the undertaking relating to UCC, his telephone 
connection shall be disconnected or provision of telecom service be discontinued 
by the Access Service Provider.

Black Carbon cloud over the country 
3263. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 whether it is a fact that scientists have warned that Black Carbon cloud over the 
country rings alarm bells; and 
 if so, the steps Government has taken to end continued dependence on coal based 
power plants and growing vehicular pollution, which has pushed the country towards an 
inevitable climatic catastrophe? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) The Atmospheric Brown Cloud (ABC) refers to the 
high loading of pollutants in the atmosphere consisting of mixture of anthropogenic sulphate, 
nitrate, organics, black carbon, dust and fly ash particles and natural aerosols such as sea salt 
and mineral dust. 
The exact impacts of pollutant loading over monsoon rain and agriculture are still under 
study and the International program on Atmospheric Brown Cloud has been initiated by the 
world community to understand such impacts. 
(b) Considering the fact that coal is to remain mainstay for generation of electricity in 
India in short to medium term perspective, new plants are being encouraged to adopt more 
efficient and clean coal tec hnologies. Besides, 1,50,000 MW hydro initiative has been 
launched to achieve the objective of full hydro potential. Non Conventional Energy sources 
are also being encouraged and 11,125 M W out of total installed capacity of 1,43,061 M W in 
the country is contributed by renewables. Measures have also been taken to improve the air 
quality and reduce the pollutant loading e.g. introduction of tightened emission norms for 
vehicle, improvement in fuel quality in transport sector, use of cleaner fuels, introduction of 
electrostatic precipitators in thermal power plants, introduction of  biogas plants and improved 
cookers in rural sector etc.

(vi) Loss of reproduction owing to disturbance on account of heavily used infrastructure

(viii) Insurgency/law and order problems 
 At present, there are 28 Tiger Reserves spread over 17 tiger States where the Project

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

global warming on various sectors. A preliminary assessment of impacts and vulnerability 
due to projected climate change in key sectors such as water, agriculture, forestry, ecosystems, 
coastal zones, health, energy and infrastructure was undertaken at the time of preparation of 
India's Initial National Communication on Climate Change submitted to the United Nations 
Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 2004. The projected climate change 
impact scenarios indicate increase in and variable trend of both rainfall and temperature into 
the 21st century, reduction in the quantity of surface run off across the various river basins,

and programmes to mitigate climate change and reduce carbon emissions. Some of the steps » 
taken by the Government include inter alia — setting up of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency 
and encouraging energy conservation and intr oduction of energy ef ficiency labeling, 
promoting use of renewable energy, power sector reforms, use of cleaner and lesser carbon- 
intensive fuel for transport, fuel switching to cleaner energy, afforestation and conservation 
of forests, promotion of clean coal technologies, reduction of gas flaring, encouraging Mass 
Rapid Transport systems and environmental qua lity management for all sectors. Besides, 
India spends every year over 2 percent of the GDP in development measures with strong 
adaptation content. 
Further, the Government has also set up an "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate 
Change" in May 2007 to study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India and to 
identify the measures that may be needed to address vulnerability to anthropogenic climate 
change impacts. 
(c) and (d) India with 16% of world population contributes to approximately 4% of global 
greenhouse gas emissions that amounts to 23.31% of USA, 30.27% of China, 37.39% of 
EU-15. 
(e) India as Party to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change ' 
(UNFCCC) has contributed to the preparation of an Action plan at the Conference held in 
Bali in December, 2007 to enable the full, effective and sustained implementation of the 
UNFCCC through long-term cooperative action, now, up to and beyond 2012. 
The Government has set up an "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate Change" in 
May, 2007 to study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India and identify the 
measures needed to address vulnerability to anthropogenic climate change impacts and any 
other matter relevant to these. 
Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change to coordinate national action for assessment 
adaptation and mitigation of climate change was constituted on 6th June, 2007 to evolve a 
coordinated response relating to climate change at the National level. The Council has decided,

climate change.

3276. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 whether it is a fact that Antarctica glaciers are melting at an alarming speed which 
may increase the water level of sea in coastal areas endangering life and property; 
 if so, details thereof; and 
 the precautionary steps that have been initiated to overcome and prevent the situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) As per NASA satellite data, the areas of 

Written Answers to [24 APRIL 2008] Unstarred Questions   71 
Antarctica where ice is increasing outnumber the areas of decreasing ice roughly by ratio of 
2:1. As per the study being conducted by the Indian Scientists in East Antarctica, the snout 
of the "Dakshin Gangotri Glacier" is receding at an average rate of 0.70 metre per annum. 
However it is difficult to quantify the ice loss from the Antarctic ice sheet as a whole, due to 
inter-annual variability and localized changes in the Antarctic sea ice extent. 
As per Fourth Assessment report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, as 
sea level rise of 24 to 48 centimetre is projected b the end of 21st Century. The projections 
include a contribution due to increased ice flow from Greenland and Antarctica, at rates 
equivalent to those observed for 1993-2003, but these flow rates could increase or decrease 
in the future. 
(c) The Government has set up a network of tidal gauges all along the Indian coast, to 
monitor the sea level. Analysis of past tide gauge records for the Indian coastline regions 
gives an estimate of sea level rise of 1.29 mm/year for the last 40 years. 
Further, the Government has set up an "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate Change" 
in May, 2007 to study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India and identify the 
measures needed to address vulnerability to anthropogenic climate change impacts and any 
other matter relevant to these.

Effluent treatment plants 
3290. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 whether many industries are polluting the river Yamuna inspite of the direction issued 
by the Central Pollution Control Board to install Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs); 
 if so, the details thereof; 
 whether the Central Pollution Control Board has expressed grave apprehensions about 
the possibility of cleaning the Yamuna river by 2010 when Delhi is scheduled to host the 
Commonwealth Games; 
 if so, Government's reaction thereto; and 
 the steps proposed to complete the project expeditiously before schedule? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) As per the information from the Central 
Pollution Control Board (CPCB), directions were issued to the State Pollution Control Boards 
of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi Polluti on Control Committee to take effective steps 
under the Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 to ensure that no effluent 
from industrial sources along river Yamuna are discharged into it without proper treatment. 
Pursuant to such directions, a total of 117 grossly polluting industries (industries discharging 
100 Kg. or more of Bio-chemical Oxygen Demand per day) were identified in the States of 
Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. Out of these, 84 units have installed Effluent Treatment Plants 
(ETPs), which are operating satisfactorily, 24 units have been closed. Nine units have installed 
ETPs but not operating satisfactorily and are facing legal action. 
(c) to (e) The CPCB is monitoring the water quality of river Yamuna and their report 
indicates that the water quality of river does not comply with the desired standards in selected 
stretches of the river including Delhi. 
Government of India has launched Yamuna Action Plan (YAP) for the abatement of 
pollution of river Yamuna with the assistance of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation 
in a phased manner. Under the phase-I of YAP launched in April, 1993,753.25 million litres 
per day (mid) of sewage treatment capacity was created, of which 30 mid in Delhi. YAP-I 
was declared closed in February, 2003. 
Under the YAP-II, which commenced in December, 2004 at an approved cost of Rs. 624 
crore, major portion of the outlay of Rs. 387.17 crore, has been allocated to Delhi. A sewage 
treatment capacity of 135 mid is to be created under YAP-II in Delhi. Besides, projects for 
the rehabilitation of 324 mid treatment capacity and rehabilitation/laying of trunk sewers of 
30.82 kms. are also envisaged under the YAP-II. 
In addition to the YAP, the Government of NCT of Delhi has also taken up large scale 
pollution abatement works for river Yamuna from its own resources. In this regard, Delhi Jal 
Board has envisaged the laying of interceptor sewers along major drains, augmentation of 
sewage treatment plants, interception of small drains, rehabilitation of trunk sewers and 
construction of additional sewage treatment plants in a time bound manner.

on the Table of both Houses of the Parliament on 7.12.2007. The policy seeks to set in 
motion a process for providing Affordable Housing for All particularly the Economically 
Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Group (LIG).

the slum dwellers/urban poor including Dalits and Minorities of identified urban areas.

infrastructural facilities for slum dwellers/urban poor in 63 select cities in the country under 
the Sub-Mission on Basic Services for the Urban Poor (BSUP). Other cities and towns are 
covered under the Integrated Housing & Slum Development Programme (IHSDP). JNNURM 
envisages a minimum of 12% beneficiary contribution, which in the case of SC/ST/Backward

features:— 
(i) Development of green belts will be developed around cities with a view to 
maintaining the ecological balance. 
(ii) Earmarking development of suitable green recreational areas like zoo, lakes 
and gardens for public visits in the Master Plan of each city/town. 
(iii) Protection of water bodies with special emphasis on keeping the flood plains of

for areas with fragile ecological char acteristics on the basis of Environment 
Impact Assessment (EIA) so as to take care of all environmental concerns at the 
planning stage itself. 
(vii) Provides encouragement to City planners to lay down norms for development 
of urban sprawls and satellite townships. 
(viii) Encouragement for preparation of State/UT level Regional Plans based on fast 
transport corridors for balanced growth.

3331. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI V. 
NARAYANASAMY): (a) No, Sir. 
 Does not arise. 
 The Planning Commission uses a poverty line based on per capita consumption 
expenditure as the criterion to determine poverty. The per capita consumption norm has 
been fixed at Rs. 49.09 per month in rural areas and Rs. 56.64 per month in urban areas at 
1973-74 prices at national level corresponding to a basket of goods and services anchored 
on a norm of per capita daily calorie requirement of 2400 kcal in rural areas and 2100 kcal 
in urban areas. The State-specific poverty lines are derived from the national level poverty 
lines, using State-specific price indices and inte r-State price differentials. This criteria now , 
being used by the Planning Commission is based on the recommendations of an Expert 
Group under the Chairmanship of Dr. D.T. Lakdawala with eminent persons in the area of 
poverty estimation as members.

Re-defining of poverty 
3340. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMAA. HEPTULLA: 
SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 whether Government is going to define poverty and bring more people under 
Government's security net; 
 if so, the details thereof; 
 whether determination of poverty is different from State to State and also different 
for 
PDS and Rural Development to provide employment under Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme; and 
(d) if so, whether Ministry would re-define poverty so that it becomes universally 
acceptable and applicable? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MI NISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI V. 
NARAYANASAMY): (a) and (b) Poverty is defined in terms of the inability to attain specific 
levels of per capita consumption and persons living in poverty are assisted by the Government 
through several programmes providing various kinds of security.  
 The methodology for determination of poverty is same for all the State. However, the 
poverty lines in the States are different, due to difference in State level prices. The estimate 
of the State-wise number of poor derived from the official estimates of poverty is used to 
allocate  foodgrain under PDS (Public Di stribution System). All rural families, i.e., both 
poor and non-poor, are eligible for employment under the National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme. The programme is demand driven and hence using the criteria of poverty 
specifically does not arise. 
 The definition of poverty being applied by the Planning Commission is based on the 
recommendations of an Expert Group consisting of eminent persons in the area of poverty 
estimation as members. The method is internationally recognized and known for its universal 
acceptability. There is no proposal to re-define poverty at present.

Instruments to check theft of vehicles 
3368. SHRI KRISHAN LAL BALMIKI: Will the Minist er of SHI PPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the specific instruments which have been made compulsory for installation by 
Government to check the day-to-day theft of the transport and non-transport vehicles; 
   (b) the existing provisions at present to cancel the licenses of drivers involved in the 
accidents and the proposals under consideration in this regard; and 
(c) the proposals received from the State Gove rnment of Rajasthan to check the road 
'accidents and also to stop the theft of vehicles and by when these proposals are likely to be 
implemented by Government? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI K.H. MUNIAPPA): (a) No specific anti-theft instrument has been 
made compulsory by the Government for fitment in motor vehicles. 
 Under Section 19 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a licensing authority may disqualify 
a person from holding a driving licence or revoke such license on a number of grounds such 
as the person being habitual criminal/drunkard/addict to any narcotic drugs or commission 
of any cognizable offence, dangerous driving etc. Under Section 22 of the Act, Court may 
also cancel the driving licence if the person is convicted of an offence relating to dangerous 
driving, causing death of, or grievous hurt to, any person. A court shall necessarily cancel 
the license on subsequent conviction for the offence relating to drunken driving. 
 Government of Rajasthan had suggested that cases of acidents by a driver be entered 
in his driving licence record and such violations should attract penalty points. The driving 
licence be cancelled after the penalty points get accoumulated to a certain level. The 
Government of Rajasthan had also suggested for making mandatory provisions in the rules 
for installation of security gadgets (central locking, steering lock, fuel lock) in the motor 
vehicles. 
The Government of Rajasthan has already been informed that issuance of driving licence 
in Smart Card mode includes provision for as many as ten endorsements on the driving 
licence along with other details. Section 19 of the Act also empowers the licensing authorities 
to disqualify a person from holding a driving licence or revoke such licence on a number of 
grounds. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 do not 
debar fitment of security gadgets in the motor vehicle.

be

 whether the State Government of Maharashtra has drawn up an ambitious Rs. 2.25 
lakh crores action plan for the makeover of Mumbai, aimed to convert India's commercial 
capital into a global financial hub;

into a global financial centre and the plan is aimed at transforming the Mumbai metropolitan 
region into a modern urban centre; 
(c) whether the World Bank has made certain suggestions in this regard;

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI AJAY  MAKEN): (a) to (e) As informed by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region 
Development Authority (MMRDA), the Government of Maharashtra undertook preparation

Transformation Project. The Vision Statement of the Business Plan is to "Transform MMR
